title: Experiencing the Queer Collective Through Time: Exploring Perceptions of Cultural and Historical Continuity Among LGBTQ + Emerging Adults
abstract: ABSTRACT Objective Using a pre‐registered explanatory sequential mixed method design, we examined collective continuity , which until now has been studied in populations where its transmission is assumed to occur naturally via familial and cultural engagement. We examined collective continuity among LGBTQ+ emerging adults for whom access to the culture and history of the collective is not always available. Method Study 1 In Study 1, we examined associations across three measures of collective continuity and their associations with LGBTQ+ identity and well‐being in college and community samples of emerging adults ( N = 246). Results Study 1 We found little association between the measures of collective continuity, modest associations between collective continuity and LGBTQ+ identity, and no relations between collective continuity and well‐being. Method Study 2 Given the lack of empirical overlap in measures of collective continuity, in Study 2 we employed a qualitative interview approach ( N = 8) to provide greater descriptive data on the phenomenon. Results Study 2 These analyses revealed a lack of collective continuity and highlighted unique factors that facilitate or forestall the development of collective continuity among LGBTQ+ people, distinguishing this process from other groups (e.g., ethnic and national) in important ways. Conclusion Together, these findings provide the opportunity for theoretical refinement and expansion of collective continuity.
